Very scary game about a journalist whose hobby is to write about scary stuff. He therefore decides to visit an asylum.

The atmosphere in this game is great, soundwise aswell as graphicwise. If you like horror, go play it!

So I drove to an insane asylum because some random dude told me that many illegal things are going on. So I brought a camera and some batteries and I went inside.

I got chased by nakey men, stabbed multiple times, hid in lockers for days at a time. I lost a couple fingers, watched a man burn himself to death, and watched a demon rip people apart.

Finally I escaped, and came home to play Outlast. Fun game btw.

The story is pretty dope, really makes you think about something... along the lines of conspiracy theories, like MK Ultra related stuff; what if there was some kind of shadowy government organization that had people locked away somewhere to perform grotesque and inhumane experiments on them? Whether for science or for their own sadistic, materialistic pleasures?
Yet another great horror game with allot of tense moments and jumpscares. Exploring the asylum and finding a way out was extremely fun. Overall another great game. Play it if you like horror :)

+ a Rocky Balboa switch

+ dark. You are forced to see with night vision, unless you like your gamma high.
+ setting
+ no wrist wrap episode

- enemies can magically disappear after chasing you
- terribly short. It took me about 5 hours to finish. I shouldn't complain, I like to bang my games and never call back.

Oh, and I remapped the crouch button to the caps lock instead of ctrl because I crouch a lot in this game and needed to be able to do it easily

I'll start off by saying this is an old game, but the lesser graphics do not take away from the experience at all, rather the eerie and gritty atmosphere they give off greatly benefits the game. Usually I find horror games and films underwhelming in terms of tenseness and scare factor but this game on more than one occasion has had me on the edge of my seat as some naked man is scowling for me. One negative I will say is each area has a similar structure, crouch around, find key, go to door/elevator, go to next area and repeat. However for a short game the narrative and story line are very well done as you piece the events together with the help of collectable documents and notes. 8/10

This game is absolutely everything you could ever want in a horror game; great atmospere, beautifully disturbing character design, brilliant attention to detail, and a storyline that will keep you guessing and completely terrified.
Outlast is such a perfect game in my opinion, despite occasional (extremely minor) glitches, and utilizes every bit of its strengths to successfully leave an impression on whoever plays it.

Pros:
-Successfully utilizes the occasional jumpscare, without doing it cheaply
-Great sounds=awesome atmosphere
-Immersion is easy; this game really messes with you psychologically!
-Situations that require strategy are believable, and not excessively difficult
-Tons of plot-twists!
-THE CAMERA MECHANIC!!! It's utilized, amazingly, in a very well-done and logical way!!!
-Every NPC is brilliantly detailed in design!

Cons:
-Several glitches
-Can cause a bit of lag on lower-end PCs
-The plot can seem a bit confusing at times
-Counts on a good ability to overcome fear in order to progress (Hard to play if you have low tolerance for horror)

All in all, if you want to play a great game that will take some decent time to finish, offers a challenge, and could possibly make you scream like a little girl, Outlast is definately the perfect game to try!! Definately worth the money, too! :)

Outlast is the most immersive survival horror game I've ever experienced. Two things to know about this game.
1. There is no fighting... at all. This is just ifne for me because stealth, hiding, running makes the game more exciting. I've played so many games where I would hit the mouse button to swing a weapon to kill something. This is well done.

2. Must be played in a fairly dark room with headphones (or a really nice sound system with the volume loud) because your survival will depend on your hearing your environment and being able to listen where things are happening. If you just run blatently out into a dark hallway, you're probably going to die.

This game. After a few minutes of playing, I was hooked until the end. AMAZING story, terrifying run-and-hide sequences, and very twisted characters. I will say there are quite a few jump scares, but Outlast definitely doesn't rely on them to keep the game scary. This is probably my favorite horror game, and I definitely plan on replaying it when I forget some of the scares to make it fresh again. If you are remotely interested in this game at all, you should definitely purchase and play it. I also completely recommend the Whistleblower DLC, which has an awesome sidestory for the game. The Whistleblower DLC also is about ten times more twisted than the main game, so there's that going for it, too. Outlast is the best, can't wait for the sequel!

There are small details that make this so good.
>When you have to hide and an enemy is near or your hide for prolonged amount of time, the protaganist's breath is so unsteady and so terrified that it sounds like he could start crying and it's so real.
>You also have camera throught nearly all of the game. Without revealing any plot points; there is an event that made me realize how important that camera is to me. I felt such love for that inanimate object becasue it is the only constant in the whole terrifying ordeal, and you don't even realize it till near the end, tbh I nearly cried. I have never felt that kind of emotion while playing a game before.
>Also, there is only 1 jump scare that I remember in the beginning of the game and another one that was obvious that I remember. I appreciate that because a game should not rely on jumpscares but atmosphere, music and art. Unlike others of this genre, this also at a point relyied on my emotions, and not just fear. My favorite game.

Outlast takes the relatively cliche setting of an asylum and manages to tell a unique story with memorable characters. The game has its share of jump scares - particularly in the first half - but it never relies on jump scares to create its oppressive environment.

Probably my favorite thing about Outlast is the enemies. From the twins to Father Martin to the Walrider, every antagonist feels different. Sure, they (mostly) all want to kill you, but their motivations and means of doing so are distinct.

I highly recommend this game to anyone who is a fan of horror.

Brilliant modern horror that takes a pretty original direction, aside from the found footage feel which has never really been done before in games. I personally think this is one of the better horror games within the past decade that is accessible to most gamers. A lot of people have some resentment for the feeling that it's a trial and error game, but I never felt that myself. It's an adventure, semi-exploration game. You have to navigate the complex halls of a mental asylum and sometimes you find death. Definitely a spooky one to pick up if you like the genre.

TL;DR: 4/5

Despite not being the most original idea (you're wandering around in an asylum) this game delivers everything it promises.
Gameplay works and feels very "natural". There are no annoying aspects to controlls or anything like that. Although there are not that many ways in which the game is trying to give you the mental breakdown you might be looking for you do get scared - terrified even.
I would definitely recomend this to fans of survival horror.

Shortcomings would be:

3. Objectives, tasks, obstackles border on repetitive. This would certainly be an issue if the game was considerably longer.

I'll be honest here. When I first bought Outlast I only managed to play 15 minutes or so, and it wasn't untill several months later that I finally managed to grow a pair and actually play. Yes, it was that scary. Everything about the game from the graphics, sound, atmosphere and story was incredibly immersive, horrifying and engaging. After beating the game I went ahead and bought the DLC and just like before, am too scared to play >.< All in all it's a solid 10/10 in my book.

I will say though that the gameplay itself did seem a bit linear or one dimensional, as all you're really doing is hiding, running or solving easy puzzles, but I'd be reluctant to list this as a criticism as I think it's simply part of the genre and further enables the user focus on atmosphere. I only mention this because, while it did not bother me in the slightest, I can see why others might be put off by the simplicity if they're looking for "complex" gameplay such as baldurs gate 2, civilization or age of empires.

It's a pretty good game which does get repetetive after a while; see when all you do is run away from random creepy characters every time you step into a new area, it loses the charm a bit each time. The mechanics are always the same and the maps, albeit somewhat different when it comes to the design, all feel the same. Regardless, it's genuinely scary and the atmosphere is insanely good.

This game is awesome.

Outlast is one of the first proper horror games I have played and wow. It sent me head first into the the horror genre. I know it's an old game but seriously its a great introduction to horror and a blast to play.
And yes it is scary.
There is nothing more panic inducing than walking down a long dark corridor with nothing but your camera and then seeing Chris Walker turn the corner and begin walking towards you and just knowing there's nothing you can do but run and hide.
The atmosphere is like nothing you have ever experienced before.
The grim aesthetic of the asylum and down right disgusting shit you see adds to it all.
Outlast is a scary, disgusting and panic inducing masterpiece and its one hell of a good time to play.

Play this game.

After reading some reviews, I decided to buy it, I played a few minutes to check it out and realized that other players were absolutely right: Outlast is terrifying, I almost fell off my chair in fear. I've never been so frightened by a game in my life, and I refuse to play it alone at night. Hats off to the developers, it's a wonderfully horrible game, with easy controls (there's not much you can do other than run, hide and clench your buttocks), great music and sound effects and an atmosphere that turns your bones to water. If you like being scared out of your wits, this is a must.

tldr.text: Overwhelmingly Positive (96%): players praise the story and characters most.
The story and characters also draw the most complaints, with some calling the defense plot terrible.

details.text: Recent reviews complain less, with story complaints at 3% of recent reviews, well below the all-time level.
Long-time players are the most positive, at 99% for those past 50 hours, while newer players are a little less so.
